page.title: Installation
page.lead: What the installation is called, where people open it and how long a build may run.

instance.title: Name and address
instance.sub: Everyone sees the name in emails and the window title. The address is used by links in emails, invitations and single sign-on.
instance.name: Installation name
instance.nameHint: For example, Department Studio or HSE Studio.
instance.publicUrlHint: The address people use to open Studio. No query string or fragment.
instance.docsUrlHint: Optional. Shown in the help menu.
instance.insecure: An http address sends passwords in clear text. Use https; http is acceptable only for localhost.
instance.urlImpact: After the address changes, links already sent in emails and invitations stop working, and the redirect URI must be updated in single sign-on providers.

issue.url_invalid: Use an address like https://studio.example.org, without parameters or a fragment.

build.title: Build
build.sub: Limits for every build on the installation's runners. Per-person and per-organization quotas are set in the Quotas section.
build.timeout: Maximum duration of one build, minutes
build.timeoutHint: From {{min}} to {{max}}. When it runs out the build stops and is marked as timed out.
build.retentionHint: From {{min}} to {{max}}. The latest result of each document is kept as long as it is needed.

page.title: Signing keys
page.lead: Whether the server may store users' secret signing keys.

signing.title: Key storage policy
signing.sub: By default the server stores no secret keys: signing happens on the user's side.
signing.toggle: Store secret keys on the server
signing.toggleHint: Users will be able to create and upload keys in settings and sign documents on the server.
signing.risks: A secret key on the server is reachable by anyone with access to the storage and the secrets encryption key. A leaked database together with that key means leaked signatures. This is usually not enough for a legally binding signature.

alt.cryptopro: Signing in the browser with CryptoPro: the key stays with the person.
alt.upload: Uploading a ready signature made outside Studio.

signing.warnOn: After you turn this on, users will be able to store secret keys on the server. Make sure the storage and the secrets encryption key are protected.
signing.warnOff: After you turn this off, users cannot create or upload secret keys, and the Signing section of their settings shows an explanation.
signing.warnOffKeys_one: The stored key ({{count}}) stays on the server but will not be used. The Signing section shows users an explanation.
signing.warnOffKeys_other: The stored keys ({{count}}) stay on the server but will not be used. The Signing section shows users an explanation.
signing.blocked_one: {{count}} key is blocked: turn storage on to bring it back.
signing.blocked_other: {{count}} keys are blocked: turn storage on to bring them back.

page.title: AI providers
page.lead: Providers everyone can use. People keep their own personal providers too.

ai.title: Shared providers
ai.sub: Connected once for the whole installation. Users see the provider and its models, but not the key.
ai.keyNote: The key is write-only: after saving, the server shows it neither to administrators nor to users.

empty.title: No shared providers yet
empty.body: Until there are some, users connect only personal providers with their own keys.

ai.deleteBody: Provider "{{name}}" disappears for every user. Agents that use it will ask to pick another one.
